It includes Python-based workflows for quantifying peaks using external standards and for interpreting unidentified peaks by generating heat maps for comparative analysis. Intracellular metabolite analysis provides a snapshot of cellular physiology under specific growth or environmental conditions, offering insights into pathway bottlenecks and reaction thermodynamics. Accurate measurement requires rapid sampling, effective quenching, and efficient extraction to preserve the in vivo metabolite state, particularly for intermediates with rapid turnover. This protocol describes the extraction of intracellular metabolites, detection of peaks in El-MAVEN from Liquid Chromatography-Mass Spectrometry (LC–MS) generated raw data files, and subsequent visualization and quantification of metabolite levels. The workflow is adaptable to diverse experimental designs, supporting both quantitative and comparative metabolomics studies in microbial systems.

Using stainless steel forceps, place the appropriate filter membrane on top of the sintered glass funnel. Rinse the filter thoroughly with Milli-Q water to remove any impurities. Use a 0.45 µm Nylon membrane for Escherichia coli, Zymomonas mobilis or for cultures grown on substrate concentrations less than 5 g/L sugars. Use a 3.0 µm Nylon membrane for Clostridium thermocellum and Thermoanaerobacterium saccharolyticum . Filter selection is critical, as the filter material significantly affects the efficiency of metabolite extraction. An ideal filter should: Retain most of the cells, Absorb minimal culture media, Filter quickly, and Be chemically inert (i.e., not react with the metabolite extraction buffer). For detailed guidance on filter selection for metabolite analysis, refer to Sharma et al., 2023. steps.title: Prepare Vacuum Filtration Unit
steps.instruction: Set up the vacuum filtration unit consisting of a conical filtration flask fitted with a sintered glass funnel connected to a vacuum pump. Wash the sintered glass funnel thoroughly using a squirt bottle before use.

steps.title: Prepare Extraction Buffer
steps.instruction: Pipette 1.6 mL of cold metabolite extraction buffer (stored at -20°C or 4°C) into a petri dish. Place the dish on a pre-chilled aluminum block maintained at -80°C or a dry ice block.

steps.title: Filter Microbial Culture
steps.instruction: Filter 3–5 mL of culture using vacuum filtration. Ensure the product of OD₆₀₀ and volume (in mL) is approximately 2.5 or higher; for cultures at OD₆₀₀ ~0.45–0.50, extract ~10 mL for stronger signal.

steps.title: Quench and Extract Metabolites
steps.instruction: Immediately transfer the filter to the petri dish, placing the cell-facing side in direct contact with the cold extraction buffer. For supernatant analysis, add 100–200 µL of clarified culture directly into the buffer.

steps.title: Homogenize and Collect Extract
steps.instruction: Gently homogenize the buffer by pipetting up and down several times with the cell-facing side of the filter facing upward. Transfer the entire volume into a 2 mL Eppendorf tube on ice.

steps.title: Clarify Extract
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the tube at 4°C to pellet cell debris and proteins. Carefully transfer the supernatant (clarified extract) to a new pre-chilled 2 mL Eppendorf tube.

steps.title: Dry Metabolite Extract
steps.instruction: Dry the required volume of supernatant using a sample concentrator (e.g., Techne EW-36620-42) with nitrogen pressure set to a maximum of 2 psi. Use needles (e.g., Fisher Scientific 3662097) inserted with the pointed side in, ensuring they do not touch the tube contents.

steps.title: Resuspend or Store Samples
steps.instruction: Resuspend the dried sample (which may appear as a gel-like substance) in HPLC-grade water immediately before use (e.g., resuspend 400 µL dried extract in 100 µL water). Alternatively, store dried samples or undried extracts at -80°C, avoiding repeated freeze-thaw cycles.

steps.title: Initialize El-MAVEN Project
steps.instruction: Launch El-MAVEN and save a project file (.emDB). Enable the 'Show Compound Widget' option to display Samples and Compounds tabs.

steps.title: Configure Libraries and Data
steps.instruction: Select the appropriate compound library from the Compounds Widget dropdown (e.g., KNOWNS, SRM2, or a custom library like 'Known BDS 2023_08_15'). Load the relevant .mzXML LC-MS data files.

steps.title: Configure Isotope Settings
steps.instruction: Click 'Isotopes' in the top panel. Select the appropriate Isotopic Tracer (C13, D2, N15, or S34) if applicable. Keep 'Report Isotopes' enabled to verify 13C natural abundance.

steps.title: Perform Peak Detection
steps.instruction: Detect metabolite peaks using one of two methods:

substeps.instruction: Automated: Click 'Peaks', select 'Compound Database Search', set Minimum Peak Intensity to 10,000 for AreaTop in the Group Filtering tab, and click 'Find Peaks'.

Manual: Select a compound from the Compounds tab, double-click the desired peak in the EIC to bookmark it, and use 'Edit peak-group' to verify and adjust boundaries across all samples (especially for closely eluting G6P, F6P, and G1P).

steps.title: Export Peak Data
steps.instruction: Export the processed data as a .csv file. Click the CSV icon in the Bookmark Table, select 'Export all groups', and choose 'Peaks Detailed Format Comma Delimited (*.csv)'. Wait up to 5 minutes for the export to complete before closing the software.

steps.title: Quantify Metabolites via Python
steps.instruction: Use the provided Python script ('2025_07_31 cthe intracellular metabolites with standards.ipynb') to quantify compounds using external standards.
